label: Jben
note: Moroccan and Algerian sources describe it as rennet-set or lactic-set depending on the maker; it sits here with rennet fresh cheeses.

about.text: A fresh, unripened cheese of Morocco and Algeria, made from raw cow's or goat's milk and traditionally drained in cloth and wrapped in palm leaves in the Rif town of Chefchaouen.

sources.text: The first paragraph of its article, shortened.
The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

how.text: Jben is the fresh cheese of the Maghreb: raw milk is set with rennet or left to curdle with its own lactic flora, the curd is ladled into cloth and drained, then salted and pressed into rounds. It is not ripened. Industrial versions use pasteurised milk, about 3 % starter and rennet added once the milk reaches 0.20–0.25 % lactic acid, with moulding at pH 4.4–4.6.

steps.note: With animal rennet (Ain Sefra: dried lamb or kid abomasum, "el Hakka"), calf rennet or a plant extract such as artichoke flower; home versions use lben.
In cloth at room temperature, overnight.

processing.text: Traditionally the raw milk curdles with its own lactic flora; industrial versions use pasteurised milk with about 3 % starter, moulded at pH 4.4-4.6. Unripened, eaten within 10-15 days.
